name: Jean-Baptiste Camille Corot
findings: Uses dark olive brown 1.7x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 945 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, dusty cornflower turns up as a small accent in 38% of the paintings that hold it, 3.6x the archive's rate (from 945 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, amber brown turns up as the lightest note in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 3.5x the archive's rate (from 945 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, cameo brown turns up as the shadow in 80% of the paintings that hold it, 3.1x the archive's rate (from 945 paintings here).
Pairs cloudy blue with pale cerulean more than chance would predict (3 of 945 paintings here).
Pairs gnaphalium green with morning blue more than chance would predict (3 of 945 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, dark olive brown, dark jungle green) covers 62% of his paintings here.
Keeps 2 distinct palette families here, from smoky black, dark olive brown to dark olive brown, smoky black.
